ygrishajev/sdlc#14.title: Publish partial work as a draft PR, and refuse workflow-file changes
ygrishajev/sdlc#14.text:
# Publish partial work as a draft PR, and refuse workflow-file changes

One part of the GitHub Actions workflow work. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below. Don't assume access to any other issue or to `docs/specs/github-actions-workflow.md`.

**Order:** builds on `jig github implement`, which already opens a ready PR for a completed run and comments when nothing changed.

## What

When a run started from an issue cannot finish but did produce changes, jig opens a **draft** PR. One PR comment lists what is still open: the reviewer's unresolved findings, final-check gaps and verification failures. If the run's changes touch anything under `.github/workflows/`, jig publishes nothing and explains on the issue that this automation cannot change workflows.

## Why

Attempts cost time and money. A run that ran out of attempts often leaves useful work and the exact list of what is wrong; throwing both away means a person starts from zero. Workflow files decide what runs with the repository's credentials, so the automation must never ship changes to them.

## Context

jig is a Node CLI (TypeScript, Vitest) that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has one agent implement and another review each slice inside a Docker sandbox, and lands them on one run branch, `jig/run/<id>`. Before editing, read `README.md`, `docs/architecture.html`, `CLAUDE.md`, and every `.claude/rules/` file that covers a file you will change, specs included.

The layering is domain rules (`src/domain/`) → flows and steps (`src/flow/`, `src/steps/`) → ports (`src/ports/`) → adapters (`src/adapters/`). Composition lives in `src/app/` and commands in `src/cli/`. Specs sit beside the code as `*.spec.ts` and pass fakes for ports, never module mocks. Anything that touches git is tested against a real temporary repository (`tests/support/temp-repo.ts`).

This issue is one part of the GitHub Actions workflow. In that workflow an operator marks GitHub issues ready, and jig, running in GitHub Actions under a GitHub App identity, implements them, opens PRs and works on review feedback. The jig core, called the *execution engine* (plan, implement, verify, review), stays independent of GitHub. The GitHub code is an *integration*: optional, jig-owned code in its own directory (`src/integrations/github/` unless one already exists). It depends on core contracts, and the core never imports it. jig must start without the integration or its credentials.

- `jig github implement --issue <n>` exists, with its GitHub port, orchestration state ref and publication receipts.
- Run state records why a run stopped: which cap was hit, on which slice, after how many attempts (`src/domain/run-state.ts`, `result.json`).
- Review feedback is free text today (`src/steps/slice.ts`); final-check results live in `src/domain/final-check.ts`.

## Target

- An outcome of `stuck` with commits on the run branch beyond the starting commit opens a draft PR (same head, base and body rules as a ready PR) plus one PR-level comment with the remaining findings, final-check gaps and the last verification failure.
- Findings are published **at PR level only**. Keep any file and line a finding mentions as text, and never invent an inline anchor. Inline placement is a later issue.
- Before any publication, check the change set (default branch fork point to run head). Any added, modified or deleted path under `.github/workflows/` means: publish nothing, comment on the issue naming the files, and record the refusal in orchestration state.
- The comment is repeatable without duplicates, through a receipt in orchestration state.

## Don't undo these

- **Agents and project commands run only inside the sandbox.** Never on the runner host, not even "for CI".
- **Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line, the image, or the sandbox.** The App key and the publishing token stay in the host process.
- **The core never imports the GitHub integration.** Dependencies point from the integration toward core contracts.
- **The host publishes, not the sandbox.** Pushes, PRs and comments are made by the GitHub integration in the host process.
- **No automatic merge.** A person merges every PR. `mergeMode` does not apply to runs this automation starts.

## Done when

- [ ] A stuck run with commits opens one draft PR and one findings comment; a rerun adds neither again
- [ ] A stuck run with no commits opens no PR and comments on the issue
- [ ] A run that changes `.github/workflows/ci.yml` publishes nothing and the issue comment names the file
- [ ] `npm run validate` passes from the repository root


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/14
